review: Fascinating, it changed the way I think about human history.
Easy to read for a non fiction book about history.
Too much speculation presented as fact, historians would disagree with a lot of it.
The idea that shared myths let humans cooperate is brilliant.
Interesting, but many claims are oversimplified.
The last part about the future drags and feels off topic.
Harari explains huge ideas in a clear and witty way.
The chapter on the agricultural revolution blew my mind.
The writing is engaging but some chapters are dense.
Great value, I learned more from this than from school history.
Very long and repetitive in the middle sections.
One of the most thought provoking books I've ever read.
Good overview, but the author's opinions creep in everywhere.
The structure from cognitive to scientific revolution makes it easy to follow.
Perfect for curious readers, I keep recommending it.
The hardcover is well made and the illustrations are helpful.
